title: Layer-Dependent Vibrational and Optical Properties of $\mathrm{Mo}{0.58}\mathrm{W}{0.42}\mathrm{Se}_2$ Alloy
authors: Szymon Socha, Tomasz Wozniak, Elena Blundo, Malgorzata Brzoska, Grzegorz Krasucki, Piotr Wrobel, Antonio Polimeni, Adam Babinski, Maciej R. Molas, Katarzyna Olkowska-Pucko
abstract: Semiconducting Mo$_x$W$_{1-x}$Se$_2$ alloys provide a versatile platform for tailoring the optical properties of two-dimensional materials through both composition and layer thickness. Here, we systematically investigate mechanically exfoliated Mo$_{0.58}$W$_{0.42}$Se$_2$ flakes ranging from monolayer (1L) to nine layers by combining Raman scattering (RS), photoluminescence (PL), reflectance contrast (RC) spectroscopy, and first-principles phonon calculations. Thirteen RS peaks are identified, including the low-frequency interlayer shear mode, whose thickness dependence is well described by a linear-chain model, yielding an interlayer force constant of $K_s=(2.996\pm0.015)\times10^{19}$ N m$^{-3}$. PL measurements reveal a crossover from the direct-bandgap 1L to indirect-bandgap multilayers. The thickness evolution of the indirect optical transition is quantitatively reproduced using a quantum-confinement model, yielding an out-of-plane reduced effective mass of $μ_\perp=0.75 m_0$. RC spectroscopy reveals four excitonic resonances. While the A and B excitons associated with the $K^\pm$ valleys remain nearly independent of layer thickness, the higher-energy C and D resonances originating from the band-nesting regions exhibit pronounced redshifts, reflecting substantial thickness-induced modifications of the electronic band structure. These results establish comprehensive spectroscopic fingerprints of flake thickness, interlayer coupling, and electronic structure in Mo$_x$W$_{1-x}$Se$_2$ alloys and provide a reliable, non-destructive framework for their optical characterization.
summary: This work provides a comprehensive spectroscopic characterization of $\mathrm{Mo}_{0.58}\mathrm{W}_{0.42}\mathrm{Se}_2$ alloys across multiple layers. By combining Raman, PL, and RC spectroscopy with theoretical modeling, the authors quantified how mechanical exfoliation tunes both the vibrational coupling and the electronic band structure. The findings establish a robust, non-destructive method for analyzing 2D van der Waals materials.
main_problem: The study systematically investigates how the optical and vibrational properties of $\mathrm{Mo}_{0.58}\mathrm{W}_{0.42}\mathrm{Se}_2$ alloys change as a function of their physical thickness.
main_result: The research established comprehensive spectroscopic fingerprints using Raman, PL, and RC spectroscopy, showing thickness-dependent changes in both vibrational modes (interlayer coupling) and electronic band structure (excitonic resonances).
method: The authors combined multiple experimental techniques—Raman scattering (RS), photoluminescence (PL), and reflectance contrast (RC) spectroscopy—with first-principles phonon calculations.
model_or_system: The physical system is semiconducting $\mathrm{Mo}_{0.58}\mathrm{W}_{0.42}\mathrm{Se}_2$ alloys, studied as mechanically exfoliated flakes ranging from monolayer (1L) to nine layers. The analysis utilizes models like the linear-chain model for interlayer coupling and quantum-confinement models for electronic structure.
key_observables: Interlayer shear mode frequency, bandgap transition (direct to indirect), excitonic resonance shifts (A, B, C, D), and the interlayer force constant ($K_s$).
important_parameters: Layer thickness (1L to 9L), interlayer force constant ($K_s \approx 3.0 	imes 10^{19} 	ext{ N m}^{-3}$), and out-of-plane reduced effective mass ($\mu_\perp = 0.75 m_0$).
main_assumptions: The linear-chain model is assumed to accurately describe the thickness dependence of the interlayer shear modes, and the analysis relies on comparing experimental data with DFT-calculated phonon dispersions.
figures_summary: Figures show room-temperature Raman spectra across various thicknesses (1L to 9L), illustrating the thickness evolution of phonon modes. Other figures detail the structural characterization via AFM height profiles and PL intensity variations.
paper_structure: The paper proceeds by first characterizing the material structure (AFM/EDX) to confirm thickness and composition, followed by detailed spectroscopic analysis. Vibrational properties are analyzed using RS and phonon calculations, while electronic properties are probed using PL and RC spectroscopy to map out thickness-dependent changes.
why_interesting: While focused on solid-state characterization, the quantitative determination of interlayer coupling constants and the modeling of quantum confinement effects in 2D materials are fundamental concepts relevant to understanding engineered quantum systems and heterostructures.
